gate: b1 decoder alone (oracle ids, oracle fp32 image_embeds -> fp16, zero-padded to 256 rows)

oracle.oracle: checkpoint decider/vision.py VisionDecisionModel.prepare() -> slot_logits(), fp32, CPU, torch.no_grad

readout: chunk order from fresh zero states (prefill S=16 while a whole chunk fits before the next slot, then S=1 up to and including it; the slot's logits from the call that processed it last), letters ids 32.. over the first nopts, softmax T=1 (float64)

bar.full_vocab_top1: the oracle's argmax letter on all slots
bar.reset: bit-equal slot logits in every process
bar.mean_of_run_mean_abs_dp_definition: mean over runs of the mean |dp| over all (slot, option) entries of the run

environment.runtime: coreai python runtime, AOT h16c GPU .aimodelc, SpecializationOptions.default(), no JIT
environment.gpu: shared with other sessions, no _GPU_LOCK (times are contended reference values)

note: The fp16 layer set [0, 2, 5] was chosen on this fixture: int8_bisect_torch.py (fp32 torch, exporter int8 weights) on rows r29 g256, r26 g448, r28 g256 and r20 g256 (logs/r6_bisect.json, rule: r29 |dp| <= 0.010 and no bisect run worse than int8lin, at most 4 layers, smallest set). r20, r28 and r29 native carry the same ids and image rows as their g256 arms. This result therefore includes the rows used in the search; generalization is checked in a later round on 250 held-out photos.

chunk_vs_s1.definition: per slot: |p_chunk - p_s1| over the question's letters (same bundle, same fixture inputs); mean_of_run_mean_abs_dp as in the bar

red_arm.arm: image_embeds zeroed (image ids and rope unchanged)

trimmed.serialization: compact json (no indentation) to keep the repository small; the full copy is pretty-printed

s1_order.readout: S=1 from fresh zero states through the whole row, logits at every slot step, letters ids 32.. over the first nopts, softmax T=1 (float64)
